model.thesis: Monitoring is one graph: every object has a URL, every count opens the sessions behind it or says why not, and every step from agent to log line and back keeps range, filters and a named way home.
principles: Aggregate on the agent (and a run's own API counts), never on session history; history shows a row count only and links up to the agent's numbers.

Every number opens the sessions behind it with the same range and filters (Agora's own rule; LangSmith and ElevenLabs are the nearest precedents). If the API cannot serve it yet, the number stays visible, disabled, with one line on why.
Every object has a URL, including panels (session, turn, log line) and derived objects (error group key <module_name>:<event_type>).
Every down pivot has a named way back: breadcrumb, scope chip, parent chip or return chip, plus a reliable Back.
Pivots narrow, never reset: going down adds one filter or overlay, going up removes it; one published key table for every level.
Inspect in a panel, own in a page: the list you came from stays underneath, untouched when you close (Retell and Vapi slide-over with chevrons and X).
Every chain ends in a confirmed change: a log line, turn or error group opens the exact setting, then Talk to agent and 'Sessions since this change with this error' show whether it came back.
Rainy states are named: unavailable is never zero, processing is never unavailable, expired is never not found, zero retention is never empty, an unlinked agent is never guessed.
Never join on agent_name: attribution to a saved agent comes only from an id (API, v2 source or the Studio session registry); otherwise the row reads 'Agent not linked'.
One component per level wherever it appears: the same session list on agent Overview, error group, run, number and history.
Selection shows in place: the chosen turn or line is highlighted with its neighbours visible, never isolated in a modal.

context_rules: Key table (one set, every level): range (24h, 7d, 30d; 90d only after the API states its lookback), from, to, widen, env (production, test, all), agent, run, number, contact, group, status, severity, module, type, direction, transport, origin, retention, new, sort, tab, q, view, via, in, session, turn, log, t, project. A level ignores keys it does not apply but keeps them in the URL, so Back restores them.

Carry rules: down pivots add one filter or overlay (from/to, widen) and a scope chip; up pivots remove the leaf and keep the rest; tab switches keep range, env, run and status and drop tab-only keys (severity, module) from display while keeping them in history.
Removing a scope chip widens the list; the breadcrumb is the way up a level.

Every tile, bucket, badge and segment pivot writes env=production. History defaults to env=all with Test tags (PRD decision 24). Recent sessions shows production plus a 'Your tests (n)' door; 'Sessions since this change' carries env=all.

Error badge unit: error groups with at least one error-severity production occurrence in range (quiet groups included and tagged); the landed Logs list under the same range and severity shows exactly that many rows; countShown rides the pivot.

Single-object pivots keep the parent range in the URL. Bucket, run-window and contact pivots are overlays with a 'Back to 7 days' chip. Up pivots from a pasted link widen the default range to include the object and say so.

Breadcrumbs are built from structural parents plus via= (agents, overview, analytics, group, run, number, config). Run: Agents / <agent> / Runs / <run>. Number: Numbers / <E.164>. A session with no proven agent: Sessions / <id>.
Back is reliable: opening a panel, turn or log pushes a history entry; Back or Esc closes the innermost; lists restore filters, sort, scroll and a 2 s row highlight.

Pages for durable objects; panels for inspection. One panel at a time: a deeper panel replaces the current one with '‹ <parent>'. in= names the list the panel steps through (group, run, number, recent, list); ↑ and ↓ follow it and 'Exit full screen' returns to it, else /sessions.
Arriving with turn=, log= or t= selects, scrolls, seeks and highlights with neighbours visible.

Deep links: /agents · /agents/:id · /agents/:id/analytics · /agents/:id/logs · /agents/:id/logs/:groupKey · /agents/:id/runs · /agents/:id/edit · /logs · /logs/:groupKey · /runs/:id · /numbers/:id · /sessions · /sessions/:id; old /agents/:id?rail=, /telephony/campaigns/:id and /agent-analytics?tab= redirect with every param kept; old group keys redirect to successors.
Copy link writes absolute from and to, project, and agent, run, number from the copier's context; a relative range is never written.
Return chip accepts only same-origin monitoring paths; unsaved builder edits ask Save or Discard; nesting stops at two levels (secret set returns to the builder, the builder returns to the source).
A pivot the API cannot serve stays visible, disabled, with one line on why (api_gap, processing, zero_retention, ephemeral, not_linked, expired, role, no_access); never hidden, never a broken link.

Retention matrix per block (metadata, transcript, recording, Analysis, events, latency) confirmed with the API team under decision 6; until then 'Retention unknown' is the default for sessions Studio did not start.
History facets carry no counts; per-facet numbers live on the agent's Analytics.
Studio session registry: a Console-backend store keyed by appid + agent_session_id holding agent_id, surface, test flag and retention for sessions Studio starts; never browser storage.

vendor_learnings.copy: Error Tracking issue panel: lifecycle up top, samples below with 'direct access to the related trace or to logs'; New and Regression tags; Deployments tab counts error types new in a version; log Trace tab rebuilds the context around one line; View in context shows neighbours even when filtered out.
vendor_learnings.avoid: The 12-tab Service page; assuming panel-over-list or tab inheritance (seen in screenshots, not documented); assuming a permalink format.

vendor_learnings.copy: Visible breadcrumb (Project / Sessions / id) over sibling session tabs; Transcript · Traces · Logs on one clock with audio playback and scrubbing; latency split into LLM TTFT, TTS TTFB, transcription delay and end-of-turn detection; data may take up to five minutes after a session ends.
vendor_learnings.avoid: No agent-to-sessions filter; dispatch errors in a CLI stream; silent rainy states; role-gated insights with no explanation.

vendor_learnings.copy: Assistant name and version shown on the session header (link unconfirmed); select a transcript line to seek the recording; chevrons and X on call detail; Assistants and Phone Numbers filter facets.
vendor_learnings.avoid: No way from an assistant's config back to its sessions; phone number is only a facet, not a page.

vendor_learnings.copy: Slide-over detail with arrows at the top and X, list state kept; transcript timestamp jumps the recording; contact conversations rail; agent id, name and version as list columns; filters in the URL.
vendor_learnings.avoid: Donut legends that need an expand before they open sessions; recording links that expire 10 minutes after the webhook without saying so.

vendor_learnings.copy: 'See conversations' carries the node filter into the list (date range carry not documented); a 'processing' status kept apart from done and failed.
vendor_learnings.avoid: Tools-tab error bars with no drill; evaluation results with no link to the criterion.

vendor_learnings.copy: Pathway name opens the pathway editor; 'Edit node' lands on the node that generated a response; one call becomes an issue and Norm Fix edits the pathway and re-verifies against it.
vendor_learnings.avoid: A hover-only session-to-config door; do not cite Bland for multi-session issue grouping (one call per issue).

vendor_learnings.copy: Issue to event with 'View More Events'; Trace-related Issue links sibling issues in one trace; a named low-sampling warning above extrapolated numbers.
vendor_learnings.avoid: Omitting sections silently when an event has no trace or breadcrumbs; opaque grouping keys.

vendor_learnings.copy: Whole view state in the URL (panes=); 'Logs for this span' carries service and time range.
vendor_learnings.avoid: Share links copy relative ranges by default, so a link shows different data later; label mismatch between levels silently returns no logs.

vendor_learnings.copy: Reverse pivot: a field in one trace builds a new aggregate query; a trace names its missing spans and links troubleshooting.
vendor_learnings.avoid: Reverse queries that land on zero rows; test every up pivot for a non-empty landing.

vendor_learnings.copy: Matching runs highlighted in place with the tree visible; chart drill in two steps (click a point to freeze, click the metric to open runs for that window); filters carried into the Any run scope.
vendor_learnings.avoid: Filters kept only as named Saved Views, not in the URL; mandatory thread grouping.

vendor_learnings.copy: Filter query serialised into the URL; project and object identity in the path (/project/{projectId}/traces/{traceId}).
vendor_learnings.avoid: Silent sampling; assuming its dashboard charts drill into traces (not documented).

vendor_learnings.copy: One phone icon on the dashboard opens Call Logs (filter carry-over not documented); events and metrics on one time axis; an Event List fallback when the timeline is dense.
vendor_learnings.avoid: Alarms and the Debugger with no link to the call that tripped them; browser Back as the only way up.

vendor_learnings.copy: returnTo on campaign detail restores list filters; agent and campaign filters survive tab switches; the call sheet already has a recording player; v2 call-history and debugging sources carry agent, campaign, numbers, has_error and session type.
vendor_learnings.avoid: Sheets held in component state; names as plain text; three time controls; v2 event ids built from page position; severity guessed from event_type.

kpis.name: Error to root cause
kpis.target: Median ≤ 4 clicks and ≤ 60 s; p75 ≤ 6 clicks and ≤ 120 s; baseline from a timed 5-owner task on the current Console; unmeasurable for sessions without v2 events
kpis.formula: Per visit (visitId, 30 min inactivity): first error_badge_clicked or error_group_opened to first log_line_opened {severity: error} in that group's session. Clicks = monitoring_pivot count; seconds = delta; median over visits that reach it; Session.message never counts. By entry and by source.
kpis.counter: Oscillation ≥ 3 times between two levels ≤ 15 %; log_line_opened left in < 5 s ≤ 30 %

kpis.name: Root cause to setting
kpis.target: ≥ 40 % of error log-line opens reach the exact setting within 10 min; median 1 click
kpis.formula: log_line_opened {severity: error} or turn_selected on a failed leg, to builder_opened {entryPoint: log_line|turn|error_group} on the same proven agent ≤ 10 min, share
kpis.counter: Wrong landing (another builder_section_opened ≤ 60 s) ≤ 20 %; agent_reverted ≤ 24 h ≤ 10 % (server diff returns changed fields to prior values)

kpis.name: Round-trip rate and integrity
kpis.target: Round trip ≥ 60 % of investigation visits (to validate); integrity ≥ 98 %
kpis.formula: Investigation visit = ≥ 1 monitoring_pivot {direction: down, toLevel: session|turn|log}. Direction from a published parent map per level; other pivots are 'across'. Round trip = same visit has an up pivot. Integrity = up pivots with stateRestored / all up pivots.
kpis.counter: time_range_changed or history_filter_changed {action: clear} ≤ 10 s after an up pivot ≤ 10 %

kpis.name: Dead-end rate
kpis.target: ≤ 10 % of level views at launch; ≤ 5 % once G4, G11 and G12 ship; by reason
kpis.formula: dead_end_viewed fires only when a disabled control is clicked or focused, or on landing on a blocked level; share of level views with no further monitoring event in 30 s; reason 'processing' excluded

kpis.name: Number to sessions
kpis.target: 100 % of counts are links or carry a disabled reason (audit); ≥ 40 % of count clicks reach session_opened in the same visit
kpis.formula: tile_clicked, error_badge_clicked or monitoring_pivot {trigger: count|tile|bucket|segment} to session_opened, same visit
kpis.counter: countShown vs history_opened.rowCount differing by > 5 % without partial=true ≤ 10 %

kpis.name: Link lands
kpis.target: ≥ 95 % of shared links open the exact object and range
kpis.formula: shared_link_opened {access: ok, found: true, rangeKind: absolute} / shared_link_opened

research.context_model: Datadog's carry-over is id-based, not URL-param-based, everywhere the docs actually describe it: a span/log/trace/RUM-session pivot works because trace_id and span_id are injected into every telemetry type via unified service tagging (service/env/version), so the destination view's search bar gets pre-populated with an id filter rather than the source page copying its own query string. One documented exception is when arriving at a nested tab already scoped to a parent (Service page -> Resources/Traces/Frontend Activity tabs): there, service+env+version+operation and the top-level time-range selector are inherited as pre-filters because the tab lives inside the service page's own chrome, not because state was copied across a navigation. Depth is handled with a floating side panel, not a full-page navigate-away, for every 'one more level of detail without losing your place' pivot: Resource click, span click in the flame graph, log-line click, issue click, and the RUM session's embedded trace view all open a panel over the existing list/graph, so 'going back' is really just closing a panel with the underlying list/search never disturbed. Only the top-level Explorers themselves (Trace Explorer, Log Explorer, Error Tracking Explorer, the Service Page) and the trace flame-graph detail are full pages. No deep-link/permalink URL format was shown or described in any of the fetched docs pages — those pages document UI interactions and query syntax, not URL structure, so that remains an unverified gap (see avoid). Time-range behavior across a cross-product id pivot (e.g., RUM session -> APM trace, or log -> trace) is also undocumented in these sources beyond the id itself anchoring what's shown; there is no stated guarantee that the destination product's time-range selector re-syncs to the source's range.

Minimum versions required (Python 1.3.0+, Node 1.0.18+); older agents simply produce no observability data, with no documented in-UI explanation of the version gap.
`record=False` at session start (or, since SDK 1.4.2, disabling audio/traces/logs/transcript individually) means those specific sub-views come up empty for that one session.
Dashboard shows the literal message 'No observability data available' for traces and logs specifically; recordings and transcript may still appear.

Data 'should populate very soon... but can sometimes take up to five minutes'; waveform/audio generation lags behind traces and logs, so a session can show partial data (e.g. logs ready, audio still pending) for a few minutes with no progress indicator described.

Project members with only Read or Write roles cannot open Insights at all; Admin role is required — implies a blocked/denied state rather than an empty-data state, though the exact denial message isn't shown.
Agent insights is LiveKit Cloud-only; self-hosting the media server removes the feature (and its UI) entirely, independent of agent SDK version.
Observability data never uploads for that session; it is simply absent afterward, with no error state surfaced in the dashboard per the sources reviewed.

All observability data — recordings, transcripts, traces, logs — is auto-deleted after a strict 30-day window; no source shows what the UI displays when opening an expired session (only that the underlying data is gone).

Explicitly excluded from the session-scoped Logs sub-tab ('you will not see any logs related to agent dispatch or job assignment'); those only appear in the separate agent-level runtime/build log stream (`lk agent logs`), with no documented link from there into any session.

avoid: Never showing (or the docs never confirming) a real, resolvable deep-link URL for a single session — only an opaque 'Copy link'/Share action exists. Our brief requires every object to have a URL; do not leave session/agent/log URLs unspecified the way LiveKit's own materials do.

Sessions list and the Agent (deployment) dashboard are only loosely joined — the Analytics API's list-sessions endpoint has no agent/room filter parameter, and no source shows a documented click from the agent dashboard into its own filtered session list. Avoid replicating that seam: the agent -> session pivot should be an explicit, pre-filtered link, not 'go search for it in the sessions list.'

The Logs sub-tab explicitly excludes dispatch/job-assignment errors (errors that have no session) from the session-scoped view, pushing them into a separate CLI-only stream (`lk agent logs`) with no link back into the dashboard. Avoid this dead end — our error groups must pivot into sessions and back even for errors that occur before/without a session.

Cross-system trace correlation depends on a developer manually setting a metadata string (e.g. `langfuse.session.id` = room name) rather than an automatic, guaranteed id. Avoid relying on an opt-in, developer-typed field for the core agent/session/log correlation key — it should be structural and automatic, not a convention someone can forget to set.

No documented search, filter, or facet system at the sessions-list level ('the documentation does not describe specific search functionality, filter options, or faceted navigation within the UI'). Avoid shipping a sessions list without search/facets — this is a real, named gap in LiveKit's own product and a place we can differentiate (per the owner's Datadog comparison).

No pivot is documented from a Trace span or a Log line back to 'the agent config that produced it' — traces/logs are session-scoped only. Avoid leaving that reverse pivot unspecified; it is explicitly required by the brief and LiveKit does not appear to support it.

Rainy states are mostly silent rather than explained in-UI (SDK-too-old, permission-denied, crash-during-shutdown, retention-expired all just present as missing/blocked data with no documented message). Avoid silent empty states in our version — give each rainy state above an explicit, worded explanation instead of a blank panel.

Breadcrumbs: neither vendor shows a literal breadcrumb bar inside the live product (Vapi's breadcrumb-looking text — "Calls > Call insights" — is the DOCS site's own nav, not the dashboard's); the dashboard instead relies on a persistent left rail (Logs > Calls tab strip) plus an open/close affordance on the detail view. Back: session detail is an overlay, not a page — Retell renders it as a right-side slide-over panel with up/down chevrons to page through sibling rows and an X to close back to the exact list state (filters and scroll position preserved); Vapi's per-call view reads as an expanded in-page section with its own header and an X, over the same Logs surface. Deep link format: not publicly documented for either vendor's exact query-string shape; the only confirmed fact is Retell's statement that "filters persist in browser storage and appear in URLs for sharing filtered views" — i.e. filtered list views are link-shareable, but no example URL is shown. Side panel vs page: Retell is a three-pane model (list -> slide-over call detail -> further right-hand contact rail) that keeps the parent list visible/dimmed; Vapi looks like a single-surface sheet (Logs page with an expanded call section) rather than a separate contact/related-sessions rail.

rainy.handling: The session row still appears with cost and latency intact, but the transcript, recording, and analysis panes are explicitly empty — operational metadata survives, content does not.
The session is still logged (time, cost, id, status) but no transcript/recording/log was ever produced for it, so the tabs that need them must show an empty/disabled state rather than an error.

Even with full storage, the recording link expires 10 minutes after the end-of-call webhook fires, so a session opened later can have transcript+logs but a dead recording control — a state distinct from full ZDR.

Concurrency and API-error-count alerts are documented as having no drill-down to a call/session at all — the alert fires with nothing to pivot into, which the design must treat as a dead-end state rather than a broken link.

rainy.state: Log stream delayed until session ends (Retell public log)

copy: Vapi's own 'Session' / 'Session logs' concept means something different from our locked 'session' noun — it groups multiple chat turns for continuity, not a single phone/voice interaction — so don't port Vapi's 'Session' label as-is; it would collide with our object model.

Both vendors use 'call' as their base noun for a voice interaction; our locked vocabulary uses 'session' for that object and reserves 'call' as a verb ('agent joins phone call'), so any ported copy needs a straight noun swap: 'call history'/'call logs' -> our own area name, 'Call Cost' -> 'Cost', etc.

Vapi's per-call tab strip ('Transcripts / Logs / Analysis / Structured Outputs / Messages / Call Cost / Latency Summary') is a ready-made tab-name pattern to adapt once the 'Call' prefix is dropped per the locked-word substitution.

Retell's alert-email copy pattern — name the workspace, the metric, and the value that triggered it, plus one dashboard link — is a clean template for our own alert copy once 'call'/'session' nouns are swapped in.

Neither vendor uses 'run' as a noun for a batch/campaign the way our locked vocabulary does; Vapi says 'Outbound Campaigns,' Retell says 'batch call' — Vapi's IA label is the closer match to port for our 'run (one API campaign)' term.
avoid: No public screenshot or doc text shows either vendor's exact deep-link URL/query-string format — do not invent one; the only sourced fact is that Retell's filtered list views are link-shareable via browser-persisted filters, with no example URL shown.
No documented reverse pivot exists from an agent-config page back to 'sessions run on this version' for either vendor — do not assume it exists; flag it as an open design decision.
No documented link exists from a session back to the specific alert/issue that surfaced it (only forward alert-to-call-history links, and only for most metrics) — do not assume a symmetric back-link.

Vapi's Monitors/Issues screen is described only in prose in monitoring-quickstart (no product screenshot was found on that page after checking) — present that flow as text-sourced, not as visually verified the way the Calls/Logs screenshots are.

Vapi's 'Session' and 'Session logs' concept (multi-chat continuity) is unrelated to phone-call monitoring and unrelated to our locked-word 'session' — do not cite it as precedent for our Sessions monitoring area.

research.context_model: Neither vendor documents an explicit breadcrumb trail; both instead lean on URL-encoded state plus browser back. Bland states outright that 'filters encode in the URL, so you can share a filtered view by copying the page URL,' and its public console URL shows the pattern directly (.../dashboard/analytics?tab=calls — tab selection itself is a query param). ElevenLabs' conversation search behaves the same way: searching a conv_… id or a text query 'stores the search mode in the URL so links are shareable and reload-safe,' and the List Conversations API mirrors nearly every list-page filter (agent_id, branch_id, workflow_node_entered_id, call_start_before/after_unix, tool_names_errored, evaluation_params, etc.) as real query parameters, strongly implying the dashboard's own URLs carry the same params. Time range is dashboard-scoped in ElevenLabs (a single date picker with preset/custom ranges that auto-adjusts chart granularity) rather than proven to travel with every pivot — the one documented cross-object jump ('View Analytics' from agent config) is only confirmed to carry agent+branch, not a time range. Session detail is a durable, id-addressable object in both products (conversation_id / call_id), not a transient side panel — it has its own sticky header, audio player and multi-section context panel, consistent with 'every object has a URL.' Sub-session structure (node inspector, expanded logs, tool-call params) is handled as in-page panels/overlays rather than route changes, reserving full navigation for the two durable levels (agent and session) plus, in Bland, the Issue/Triage object. Reverse pivots are the weakest-documented part of both products: only the session→pathway-editor hover action (Bland) and the issue→originating-calls list (Bland) are explicit; ElevenLabs has no documented reverse link from an evaluation result or a Tools-tab error bar back to its configuration or to the erroring sessions.

rainy.handling: ElevenLabs conversation status is one of initiated, in-progress, processing, done, or failed — 'processing' is the documented state where the transcript exists but evaluation_criteria_results / data_collection_results are not ready yet; sources don't specify the exact placeholder shown in that column, only that the status field itself distinguishes it from done/failed.

rainy.state: Zero Retention Mode — no transcript/audio/PII ever stored
rainy.handling: The conversation still exists as a metadata record (duration, cost, status) but 'log and transcript storage features are unavailable for this request'; only a reasoning summary can still reach a post-call webhook or chat client, so the session-detail transcript/analysis panels have nothing to show by design, not by failure.

Docs state that 'reducing the retention period may result in immediate deletion of data older than the new retention period' but do not describe what the history UI shows for a purged row (tombstone vs. disappearance) — an explicit gap in the sources, not something to invent.

Bland's call-logs table only renders the play/download Action buttons 'when recordings exist'; when a call wasn't recorded (or recording failed) the actions are simply omitted rather than replaced with an explicit empty-state message.

rainy.state: Errors that don't yet belong to any session-linking object
rainy.handling: Bland's Alerts fire on aggregate thresholds (e.g., percentage of calls with API errors within a 10-minute–24-hour lookback) rather than pointing at one call; the bridge from 'a problem exists' to 'these are the sessions that show it' is the separate, manual/AI-assisted 'Flag for triage' step, which is the point where originating calls and the pathway get auto-attached as evidence.

rainy.state: Tool-call errors inside an otherwise normal session
rainy.handling: ElevenLabs treats a tool error as a filter (tool_names_errored) on the session list rather than a distinct rainy-state screen — the erroring tool call still renders inline in that conversation's transcript/tool-call log.
Not documented in either vendor's public docs found; do not assume either product samples — flagged as an open question for direct vendor confirmation rather than invented.

avoid: Don't rely on hover-only affordances for the one reverse pivot that matters most (session → the config that produced it): Bland's 'navigate to the generating node' only exists as a hover action on a transcript bubble, easy to miss and impossible to deep-link to.

Don't drop filters, ids, or time range when pivoting down or back up — both vendors treat the list's filter state as URL-encoded and shareable; a pivot that resets the segment breaks the 'every number opens the sessions behind it' promise.

Don't render a 'processing'/analysis-pending session identically to a failed one — ElevenLabs' own status vocabulary (initiated/in-progress/processing/done/failed) exists precisely to keep those apart; collapsing them removes the rainy-state signal.

Don't make a single error a dead end — Bland's model only becomes useful once an error is attached to a real, multi-call Issue object (severity, owner, originating calls, pathway); a red cell with no path to 'how often, and where' repeats ElevenLabs' documented gap (Tools-tab error bars have no drill-down into the erroring sessions).

Don't turn every intermediate inspection into a full page/route change — both vendors keep node inspectors and expanded per-turn logs as in-page panels, reserving real navigation (and a URL) for the two durable objects, agent and session (plus Issue, in Bland).

Don't ship 'aggregate on the agent, never on session history' without defining what a zero-retention or retention-expired session looks like in the list/detail — neither vendor's docs specify this, and an undefined state here is exactly where the agent→session promise would silently break.

research.context_model: All three vendors treat the primary object id (trace id, span id, issue fingerprint, release version) as something embedded directly in the destination's query or URL, never something the user re-enters. Sentry and Honeycomb additionally carry the *whole* originating query state (search filter, environment, date range, WHERE clauses) forward into every deeper view, substituting only the newly-selected id -- so a pivot narrows scope rather than resetting it. Grafana goes further and encodes full per-pane state into the page URL itself (`/explore?panes=<json>&schemaVersion=...&orgId=...`, each pane holding its own datasource, query and absolute from/to in milliseconds), which is what makes deep-linking, bookmarking and its split-view time-sync possible; very long encoded URLs get a `/goto/:uid` shortener that still resolves to an absolute (not rolling) time range so recipients see identical data. When two datasources don't share a native join key, Grafana's Correlations feature does explicit variable interpolation (`${field}` extracted from a log line or table cell substituted into a differently-shaped target query) rather than relying on identical field names; the traces<->logs/profiles pivots that *don't* go through Correlations instead rely on exact, case-sensitive label parity between systems (service.name vs service_name), which is the single most-cited failure point in Grafana's own docs. Time range is otherwise treated as a rolling window that a pivot either keeps (issue -> event, query -> trace) or pins to a point-in-time (trace -> logs, exemplar -> trace, both of which narrow to the span's own start/duration).

research.context_model: Both vendors keep a single project/table as the anchor and open detail as a side panel or in-place expansion rather than a full page swap, which is what keeps 'every step in between' reachable. Langfuse: the Traces/Observations tables share one filter state between a sidebar filter builder and a one-line filter search bar (bidirectional sync), and that whole query string serializes into the URL, so a shared link reproduces the exact filtered view; object identity is carried as path segments (/project/{projectId}/traces/{traceId}, /project/{projectId}/users/{userId}) rather than query params, and a trace can be flipped to 'public' to be viewed without login. A dashboard's selected view is likewise reflected in its URL. Session→trace→observation is a strict containment drill (click deeper, tree/breadcrumb-style link back up via a badge on the child), not a modal/panel. LangSmith: the project view exposes a persistent filter toolbar (scope selector + search + time range + table switcher + Save View) whose state a monitoring-chart click can override with a time-bin filter; opening any row keeps that filter and highlights matches instead of losing them. Detail is a right-hand side panel with three toggleable lenses (Trajectory/Turns/Details) over the same underlying thread, switchable with single-key shortcuts (T/D) with no navigation cost, and the run tree on the left of Details stays fully rendered so the selected run's context (parent/sibling runs) never disappears — there is no separate 'go back up' action because you never left. Deep links exist at the trace/run level (https://smith.langchain.com/public/{trace-id}/r for public shares; project + tab query params for authenticated views) but LangSmith's docs do not state that an arbitrary filtered table view serializes into a shareable URL the way Langfuse's does — it instead persists filters as a named 'Saved View'.

rainy.handling: If a trace is not sampled, none of its observations or scores are sent at all — it simply never appears; there is no placeholder or 'sampled out' marker documented.

Traces/observations/scores past the configured retention window (min 3 days, Pro/Enterprise/self-hosted only) are deleted by an asynchronous nightly job — permanently and without recovery; a trace can outlive its window by up to 24h before the job runs. Saved dataset items and audit logs are exempt.

Docs explicitly warn this is often not a bug: the root observation already carries the same input/output, so an apparently empty trace-level field doesn't mean data loss — check the observation before assuming ingestion failed.
Documented first cause to check is the dashboard/table time filter being narrower than when the trace was created — the data was ingested but hidden by the current view, not lost.

sessionId is optional metadata set at trace creation; a trace created without it simply never appears under any Session and stays a standalone row in the Traces table — there is no forced session grouping.

The Threads tab and the Turns view require a thread_id (or session_id) metadata field; without it the run still shows individually in Traces/Runs, but there is no thread grouping and no Turns/Trajectory view for it — the direct analogue of an 'error without a session.'

An 'incomplete' status means the trace's end event was never received (tracing runs on a background thread that can die before flushing) — the run stays visibly unresolved rather than silently disappearing.

At high request volume, especially on free-tier, the ingestion queue can silently drop events, and traces can lag behind real time; documented mitigation is explicit sampling (log every Nth request) or upgrading plan — the UI itself gives no built-in 'stream delayed' indicator in the docs reviewed.

SaaS trace retention is capped (max lowered to 180 days as of Sep 2026, selectable 30–180d); once deleted, docs state there is no recycle bin/undo. Self-hosted TTL defaults to 400 days long-lived / 14 days short-lived, cleaned by a weekend cron job.

rainy.state: [LangSmith] Alert firing with sparse/no qualifying data
rainy.handling: Not explicitly documented; the Alert Preview lets you check historically which datapoints would have breached a threshold before turning it on, which is the vendor's substitute for a live empty-state warning.

research.context_model: Twilio carries context in two different ways depending on whether the destination is a page or a panel. Dashboard → Call Logs is a real navigation that inherits the dashboard's Time Range Picker value and every active Filter Builder dimension (documented as 'the call logs view helps you drill down into a subset of calls with specific issues'), so the list opens pre-scoped rather than empty. Call Logs → Call Summary drops those list-level filters entirely and re-keys the whole page to one identifier, the CallSid — deep links are SID-addressed throughout the platform (the REST mirror of this is literally GET https://insights.twilio.com/v1/Voice/{CallSid}/Summary, and the Console path is documented only as a static breadcrumb-like menu route, Monitor > Insights > Voice > Calls / Monitor > Debugger / Monitor > Alerts > Alarms, not as a URL pattern). Inside one Call Summary, the Details/Insights Summary/Metrics tabs and the Event Stream/Event List and SDK/Twilio-Gateway sub-toggles are all in-page state changes on the same CallSid — no navigation, no new history entry, and therefore no back button needed (you just click the other tab). Detail-on-demand elsewhere (Debugger log rows, Alarm Logs rows) uses a slide-over side panel rather than a page change, which is why the underlying filtered/searched list is still there, untouched, when the panel is closed — that panel-over-list pattern is Twilio's substitute for a breadcrumb. Nowhere in the documented UI is there an explicit breadcrumb trail (Dashboard > Calls > Call NNN); 'going back up' relies on browser Back for real page navigations and on closing a panel for everything else.

rainy.state: call still in progress / incomplete summary
rainy.handling: the Call Summary renders with partial data rather than blocking — 'incomplete summary details are available while the call is in-progress,' with full aggregation taking up to 30 minutes (partial record within ~10 minutes via the API); the Metrics tab additionally exposes an explicit 'Enable Auto Refresh' toggle for exactly this state.

documented plainly as a compliance limit — 'To comply with GDPR, Twilio stores Voice Insights data only for 30 days' — and the Debugger is separately capped at the same 30 days; no in-UI 'data expired' empty-state copy is documented for either surface, data past the window simply isn't returned.

metrics are not continuous: Voice SDK calls are sampled every 1 second, Carrier/SIP calls are sampled as cumulative stats over the previous 10 seconds every 10 seconds — the graphs are drawn from these fixed-interval samples, not raw packet-level data.

long or network-troubled Voice SDK calls can produce 'hundreds of events'; the Event Stream (visual timeline) degrades by showing only a 'portion' of event titles/timestamps while keeping every dot selectable, while the Event List (table) never truncates and shows all events ordered by timestamp — density is traded off in the visual view, completeness is preserved in the tabular fallback.

rainy.state: errors without sessions (aggregate alert, no specific request)
rainy.handling: Alarms fire on an error-code count crossing a threshold within a time window, not on any single request; the Alarm Logs side panel exposes only the error code, an error-history chart, and a link to the public Error and Warning Dictionary — there is no documented link from an alarm to the specific CallSid/request that tripped it, so the person has to separately search the Debugger by error code and time window.

rainy.state: stream delayed (Event Streams / Kinesis / webhook sink)
rainy.handling: not documented — the Event Streams page describes Call Summary Complete events as an async fan-out to Kinesis/webhook/Segment sinks but publishes no latency/SLA figure and no in-Console indicator of sink lag; delay would only be visible from the receiving system's own timestamps.

the Debugger's Log properties panel includes the Request Inspector section only 'if applicable' — for debug events not tied to a webhook request, that section is simply omitted rather than shown empty or broken.

avoid: Don't let an aggregate alert dead-end at a count: Twilio's Alarms fire on an error-code threshold with no documented link to the specific call/session that tripped it, forcing a manual re-search in a separate tool (the exact 'errors without sessions' failure the brief calls out) — every Agora alert should carry a direct pivot into its session.

Don't rely on browser Back as the only way up: nothing in Twilio's documented Dashboard / Call Logs / Call Summary / Debugger / Alarms flow shows an explicit breadcrumb trail; Agora's own rule (every object has a URL, reverse pivots must exist) is stricter than what Twilio ships and shouldn't regress to it.

Don't split call-quality monitoring and error/warning monitoring into two uncorrelated surfaces the way Twilio splits Voice Insights from the Debugger — a single bad call can produce entries in both with no cross-link between them; keep Agora's agent-monitoring and sessions views cross-linked in both directions instead.

Don't let a retention window expire silently: both Twilio surfaces are hard-capped at 30 days with no documented 'data expired' empty state; Agora's zero-retention/ephemeral-session states should render an explicit message rather than just returning nothing.
Don't cap an export with no in-UI explanation: Twilio's CSV export silently stops at 2,000 rows; if Agora caps an export, say so in the UI at the point of export.

Aggregation instead lives on a separate, project-wide /agent-analytics page's Monitor tab: recharts KPI area/pie charts (useTelephonyAnalyticsSummaryQuery) filterable down to one agent via agent_uuids. No golden-signals header and no rolled-up error/warning badge exist anywhere.

levels.shows: Inside the session sheet's Events tab: a module/level-filterable, paginated event list (EventsTabPanel). Latency tab shows per-leg timing (LatencyTabPanel). There is no raw request/response JSON toggle per event, and no link from a log line back up to the specific agent config version that produced it.

research.context_model: Time range: NOT one global control. The Monitor tab has its own date_range (7/30/90/custom) driving useTelephonyAnalyticsSummaryQuery; Call History has a separate time_filter (24h/1w/1m/3m/custom); Session History has its own session_time_preset. Switching tabs keeps agent/campaign selections but not a single shared clock, unlike the one-global-time-range model observability-patterns.md recommends. Breadcrumbs: only the agent builder route renders a Breadcrumb (with an inline save-status indicator); campaign detail substitutes a returnTo search param instead of a visible trail; call/session detail sheets have no breadcrumb since they are overlays, not routes. Back: campaign detail's Close button decodes returnTo to restore the list's exact filters; call/session sheets rely on onOpenChange(false) collapsing React state, so browser Back does not reliably reopen or close them (no history entry is pushed when they open). Deep link format: Agent (/agents/$agentId) and Run (/telephony/campaigns/$campaignId) are canonical path-param routes with query-string sub-state (rail, tab, section, sheet, returnTo); Call History/Session History are query-string-only list views on the shared /agent-analytics path (tab, agent_uuids, campaign_ids, date_range, etc.). Side panel vs page: Agent and Run are full pages; Call and Session detail are always right-side Sheets over the list, at one depth only (no separate 'full session' page beyond the sheet), so pasting the current URL never reopens the specific call/session that's open.

rainy.handling: No UI treatment exists in ng-console today. observability-patterns.md recommends rendering it as a normal row (so totals stay correct) with an explicit 'zero data retention' message replacing transcript/audio on the detail page, never a silently blank panel; v3's data_policy field (object-model.md, gap G7) only exists on session create today, so inbound/batch sessions have nowhere to read a retention flag from yet.

rainy.state: Ephemeral session with no saved agent
rainy.handling: POST /sessions/ephemeral takes an inline agent, so the session has no agent_id to backlink to. competitor-monitoring.md notes no vendor documents this state either. Console's CallDetailSheet keys its row identity off `${callId}-${agentId}` (call-detail-sheet.tsx), so an agent-less session needs a new 'no agent to open' treatment rather than a broken link.

Already modeled as flat, filterable facets (HISTORY_CALL_CATEGORY_OPTIONS in telephony-page.tsx, split by inbound/outbound), but there is no grouped 'error group' view - each outcome is a filter value a user must already know to pick, not a surfaced, counted issue.

rainy.state: A specific call/session opened via a shared link
rainy.handling: Not supported. Only the tab-level filters (agent, campaign, date range, tab) live in the URL on /agent-analytics; the individual call/session sheet is local component state (selectedCall/selectedSession), so a colleague opening a pasted link lands on the filtered list, never on the specific row that was open - matches observability-patterns.md's 'un-shareable state' anti-pattern and v3 gaps G4/G5 (SessionListItem/Session don't return enough fields to reconstruct a detail deep link from the API alone).

ConsoleEmptyState/QueryState primitives are used generically across these tables; per the project's quiet-chrome rule this should say so plainly rather than show a zeroed chart, which matches observability-patterns.md's own recommendation for this exact case.

copy: Locked v3 vocabulary: agent, session (never 'call' as the API/UI noun for the general unit - reserve 'call' for telephony-modality sessions specifically), run (one API campaign), deployment, integration, error group, test vs production, zero retention, ephemeral session, Analysis.

Retired words per prd-v3.json funnel.conflicts: connection, connect, connector, channel (alone), publish, deploy (as a verb), live (except the phrase 'Go live'), call (except literal API names), modality (in UI), tier, template, own key, inline agent, quota, error dot, Personalisation.
Post-call extraction is named Analysis in the UI (the API field is structured_output) per object-model.md's naming map - do not call it Monitoring or Variables.
One API campaign = UI Run; a grouping of runs (a 'Campaign' in the UI sense) has no API entity yet - object-model.md flags this as a Studio-only concept until the API adds one.

Word the health/error badge as counts ('2 errors, 3 warnings'), never as reassurance or a green checkmark - matches both observability-patterns.md's anti-pattern list and the project's own quiet-chrome rule against ticks meaning validation.

Naming for 'deployment' changed: object-model.md's old UI label 'Deployment . Channel' mapped to API 'transport' is superseded - the fix doc in prd-v3.json points it at Number.inbound, Campaign, and POST /sessions instead; 'Transports' stays an internal-only name, the user-facing page is Numbers.
avoid: Session/call detail opens as a right-side Sheet driven by local React state (selectedCall/selectedSession in call-history-route-module.tsx), not a route - no shareable or refreshable URL per session, unlike Run which does have a canonical /telephony/campaigns/:campaignId.

Agent builder (/agents/$agentId) has no analytics/sessions/logs tab in its section rail (tab is one of prompt|models|advanced|actions|custom-config|agent|tools|knowledge) - monitoring lives entirely on a separate /agent-analytics page disconnected from the builder's URL.
/agent-analytics is one project-wide page merely filterable by agent_uuids, not an agent-owned page - there is no per-agent canonical monitoring URL (e.g. /agents/:agentId/sessions).

Call detail sheet shows campaign name and agent name as plain text (call-detail-sheet.tsx, CallDetailSummaryRow around the 'campaign' field), not as clickable links back to the run or the agent - no session-to-run and no session-to-agent backlink today.

No error/issue grouping exists anywhere in ng-console: call/session outcomes (failed, no_answer, voicemail, transferred) are flat filterable facets (HISTORY_CALL_CATEGORY_OPTIONS in telephony-page.tsx) with no Sentry/Datadog-style fingerprinted error group or count-based drill-in.
No golden-signals or health badge exists on the agent or agent-analytics page - KPI charts exist on the Monitor tab, but nothing rolls errors up into a single clickable badge.
Session detail's Events tab (session-detail-sheet.tsx) has no raw request/response JSON toggle per event, and no link from a log line back up to the specific agent config version that produced it.

Phone number pages (telephony/phone-numbers) have no visible link forward into the sessions/calls that number has carried - the Number-to-Session pivot is missing, consistent with v3 gap G4 (SessionListItem has no phone-number field to filter or join on).

v3 API gap G4: SessionListItem returns start_ts/status/agent_id only, and Session itself returns agent_name rather than agent_id - a UI can't reliably reconstruct a detail deep link from list data alone.

v3 API gap G5: client_reference and data_policy are never returned by the API, so a session's origin, retention mode, and agent source are unknown unless Studio itself recorded the ids at creation time.

v3 API gap G2: session_ended {agent_id, agent_session_id, duration_s, status, end_reason, turn_count, ...} has no owner/emitter yet, so inbound/code 'answered' and error-acknowledgement stages are unmeasurable until it ships.
v3 API gap G7: data_policy (retention) exists only on session create, not on Number.inbound or Campaign - a zero-retention badge on an inbound or batch deployment has no field to read from yet.
v3 API gap G6: no integration health field exists (no MCP handshake status, no tool execution log) - an agent-to-integration error linkage has no data source in the spec today.

Rows can now probably open detail. Joining on agent_name is banned.

Added a launch status (live, partial or disabled) to every pivot, plus a v2-backing decision that extends PRD decision 15 and is paired with PRD decision 5 (blocking, Mon 28 Sep). Chains are labelled 'after Gx', and a v3-only launch chain now ends at Status detail.

Added a project-level Logs view (/logs) with 'No agent' and 'Agent not linked' buckets, a project error badge, and an Integration level (disabled until G6 ships). Sessionless, ephemeral and deleted-agent errors now have somewhere to appear.

Error groups: the key is now <module_name>:<event_type>, always marked approximate. Severity is derived, and there is a no-warnings state. Added New, Quiet, Returned and New-since-change tags, a last-change marker, and 'Since your change: N occurrences'. The badge unit is defined as error groups, with count parity to the Logs list.
Log lines are keyed by lts plus a hash, because v2 ids are built from page position. Session.message moved to a 'Status detail' header field and no longer counts as a log line or toward any KPI.

Turn to log is disabled until the turn.finished join is verified on 20 sessions. Latency legs are redefined as end-of-turn detection, transcription delay, LLM TTFT, TTS TTFB and end to end, with 'Not measured yet' for missing legs. Transcript is disabled for RTC and code sessions.

Session detail gains a Recording block on the shared clock (seek, ?t=, Download audio). Added Processing, Running, role-restricted, Retention unknown and 'Agent not linked' states. Zero retention now shows only when a source says so.

Runs: counts are contact states. Calling and completed open sessions, failed opens contacts, and pending and canceled never link. Pause has no reason, the agent name is cached, from-number chips are a list, and the Runs tab appears when runs exist.

Secret set pivot and the 'since this change' clock: the secret set is a Studio label recorded at save, 'Sessions since this change' uses SecretSet.updated_at for secret fixes and a config-changed label for agent fixes, and the banner now reads 'Agent saved after this session'. The fix loop confirms with 'Sessions since this change with this error'.

Run window, bucket and contact are overlays. in= lets arrows step through group, run and number lists. Breadcrumbs now include via= and fallbacks. The return chip only accepts same-origin paths. Presets are capped at 30 d.
